stem:
The hydrogen halides, $\text{HCl}$, $\text{HBr}$ and $\text{HI}$, can undergo thermal decomposition. In a sealed container an equilibrium is established according to the equation shown.

$$2\text{HX(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{X}_2\text{(g)} \quad \text{(where X = Cl, Br or I)}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Some bond energies are shown in the table.

|  | bond energy / $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{H-Br}$ | 366 |
| $\text{H-H}$ | 436 |
| $\text{Br-Br}$ | 193 |

Use these data to calculate a value for the enthalpy change, $\Delta H$, for the thermal decomposition of hydrogen bromide, $\text{HBr}$, according to the equation shown.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Using the same axes, sketch a second curve to indicate the Boltzmann distribution at a higher temperature.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: With reference to the curves, state and explain the effect of increasing temperature on the **rate** of decomposition of $\text{HBr}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The decomposition of $\text{HBr}$ is endothermic.

State the effect of increasing temperature on the **percentage** of $\text{HBr}$ that decomposes. Use Le Chatelier's principle to explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
At $700\text{ K}$ $\text{HBr}$ is approximately 10% decomposed but hydrogen iodide, $\text{HI}$, is approximately 20% decomposed.

Explain this difference with reference to bond strengths and the factors that affect them.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
At temperatures above $1500\text{ K}$, $\text{HCl}$ will decompose.

A sample of $0.300\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$ decomposed in a sealed container.

The resulting equilibrium mixture was found to contain $1.50 \times 10^{-2}\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Cl}_2$.
parts.text: Calculate the amounts, in mol, of $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ present in the equilibrium mixture.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the mole fraction of each gas in the equilibrium mixture.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
In another experiment under different conditions, an equilibrium mixture was produced with mole fractions for each species as shown.

| species | mole fraction |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{HCl}$ | 0.88 |
| $\text{H}_2$ | 0.06 |
| $\text{Cl}_2$ | 0.06 |
parts.text:
Write the expression for the equilibrium constant, $K_p$, for the decomposition of $\text{HCl}$.

$$2\text{HCl(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$$

$K_p =$

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the total pressure of the system does **not** need to be known for $K_p$ to be calculated for this experiment.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the value of $K_p$ for this experiment.
